newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- April 30.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Wednesday:
* Employers were told by the U.S. government they could not discriminate against qualified workers with mental illnesses or ask those applying for jobs if they had a history of mental illness.
* The stock market soared higher as a major economic indicator which measured labor costs did not show inflationary signs despite a strong economy.
* A key U.S. government witness against Timothy McVeigh recounted to a Federal Court jury how McVeigh told her of his plans to blow up the Federal Building in Oklahoma City.
* A U.S. Army sergeant was found guilty by a military jury of 18 counts of raping female subordinates.
* British Prime Minister John Major is still campaigning across Britain despite polls which show the ruling Conservative Party is as much as 20 points behind Tony Blair's Labor Party.
* A group of orphan children who were taken out of Sarajevo in August 1992 and given refuge in Germany have returned to the Bjelave orphanage but face a bleak future.
* Rwandan Hutu refugees in Zaire are providing accounts of machete, axe and gun attacks they suffered there.
